open_points.subject: supported Linux baseline
open_points.text: The service runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named
open_points.question: Which Linux kernel, distribution, libc, and file-system versions define the supported baseline?
options: Support every Linux version whose relevant calls exhibit the required semantics
Name a minimum kernel and libc version
Publish a tested distribution and file-system matrix
open_points.default_guess: Name a minimum kernel and libc version and a tested file-system set.

witness.initial: A host runs Linux, but its kernel or libc predates the baseline one implementer would select.
events: A deployer installs the service on the host.
The service uses one of the listed file operations.
outcomes: The host is supported because the text names Linux without a version.
The host is unsupported because the implementation assumes a newer Linux baseline.
witness.observer: the deployer and users of that installation

open_points.subject: environment support determination
open_points.text: a Linux or file system on which a call these rules rely on ... does not act as Linux documents it, is unsupported: the service neither tests for it nor defines what it does there
open_points.question: Who determines before deployment that the host and file system provide the required behavior, and by what operation or evidence?
options: The deployment route performs a compatibility check
A release process certifies a published platform matrix
The operator is responsible for verifying compatibility
No one verifies it; incompatibility is discovered only at runtime
open_points.default_guess: Have the release process certify a published platform matrix and make the deployment route accept only that matrix.

witness.initial: The service is being deployed on Linux using a file system whose behavior has not been certified.
events: The deployment process must decide whether to proceed.
outcomes: Deployment proceeds because running Linux is treated as sufficient.
Deployment is refused because conformance has not been established.

open_points.subject: Linux-dependent file-operation flows
open_points.text: opening without following a link, opening a folder as a folder, opening without blocking, creating exclusively, locking, renaming, flushing
open_points.question: For each listed behavior, which flow requires it, which module operation provides it, who calls that operation, and what outcome each possible failure produces?
options: Expose separate module operations for each listed behavior
Expose higher-level atomic storage operations that encapsulate several behaviors
Treat the behaviors as uncontracted implementation details of an existing operation
open_points.default_guess: Define higher-level storage operations that encapsulate the required Linux calls, name their callers, and distinguish conflicts or unsafe paths from unexpected I/O failures.
